Lesson / Topic: for, since, from – what's the difference?
Core idea: For, since и from показват продължителност или начало на период, но отговарят на различни въпроси.
Main rule / explanation: For = duration. Since = starting point continuing to now/another reference time. From = starting point, често с край или диапазон.
Form / structure: for + length. since + starting point. from + starting point (+ to/until).
When / why we use it: For отговаря на „колко дълго?“. Since — „от кой момент?“. From често образува диапазон.
Examples:
I've lived here for five years. → Живея тук от пет години.
I've worked here since 2021. → Работя тук от 2021 г.
The office is open from nine to five. → Офисът е отворен от девет до пет.
Special cases / exceptions: Не бъркай duration и starting point.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've lived here since five years. → ✅ I've lived here for five years.
❌ I've worked here for 2021. → ✅ I've worked here since 2021.
Don't confuse with: for = amount of time. since = starting point. from = starting point/range.
Quick summary / memory hook:
for = how long.
since = from when.
from = starting point, often + to.

Core idea: В английския има различни типове въпроси според това каква информация липсва и какво искаме да подчертаем.
Main rule / explanation: Yes/No questions обикновено започват с auxiliary/modal. Wh-questions започват с question word. Ако who/what е subject, do/does/did обикновено не е нужен. В everyday English предлогът често отива накрая.
Form / structure: Yes/No: auxiliary/modal + subject + verb. Wh: question word + auxiliary/be + subject + verb. Subject question: Who/What + verb. Preposition: Who are you talking to?
When / why we use it: Избирай структурата според вида на въпроса и според това кой извършва действието.
Examples:
Do you work here? → Работиш ли тук?
Are they waiting for us? → Те чакат ли ни?
Where do you work? → Къде работиш?
Who called you? → Кой ти се обади?
Who did you call? → На кого се обади?
Who are you talking to? → С кого разговаряш?
Special cases / exceptions: По-официалният стил допуска preposition пред whom/which: To whom are you speaking? В everyday English по-често Who are you speaking to?
Common mistakes:
❌ Where you work? → ✅ Where do you work?
❌ Who did call you? → ✅ Who called you? (when who = subject)
❌ What are you looking? → ✅ What are you looking for?
Don't confuse with: Първо попитай: какво е неизвестно — subject, object, place, time и т.н.? Това подсказва структурата.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Yes/No → auxiliary/modal first.
Wh-question → question word first.
Who/what as subject → usually no do/does/did.
Preposition often goes to the end.

Core idea: Indirect question е по-вежлив и по-малко директен начин да поискаме информация. Особено полезен е в работа, обслужване и formal conversations.

Don't confuse with: Не бъркай direct question word order с embedded question word order.
Quick summary / memory hook:

Core idea: Auxiliary verbs помагат при въпроси, отрицания, emphasis и различни времена. Главните auxiliaries са be, have и do. Modal verbs също работят като auxiliaries.

Core idea: Narrative tenses помагат да разкажем история: какво е станало последователно, какво е било в процес, какво е станало по-рано и колко дълго е продължавал процесът.

Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Комбинирай времената, за да стане ясно как са свързани събитията.

She was tired because she had been working all night. → Тя беше уморена, защото беше работила цяла нощ.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect не е нужен автоматично за всяко „по-ранно“ действие. Използвай го, когато е важно да покажеш relationship with another past point.
Common mistakes:

❌ She had been work all night. → ✅ She had been working all night.
Don't confuse with: Мисли за timeline: main event, background, earlier event, duration before earlier point.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main sequence.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.

Lesson / Topic: Position of adverbs and adverb phrases

Core idea: Future Continuous показва действие, което ще бъде в процес в конкретен момент в бъдещето. Future Perfect показва, че действието ще е приключило до даден бъдещ момент.

Lesson / Topic: Used to, be used to, get used to

Quick summary / memory hook:
used to + V1 = past habit/state.
be used to + noun/-ing = familiar now.

Lesson / Topic: Would and used to – past habits and repeated actions
Core idea: Used to и would могат да описват повтарящи се действия в миналото, но used to може да описва и минали състояния.
Main rule / explanation: Would работи добре в разкази за repeated past actions. Used to е подходящ и за repeated actions, и за past states.
Form / structure: used to + V1. would + V1 за repeated past action.
When / why we use it: Повтарящо се действие: When I was a child, I would visit my grandparents every weekend. Past state: I used to live in Kyiv.

When I was a child, I would visit my grandparents every weekend. → Когато бях дете, ги посещавах всеки уикенд.
I used to live in Kyiv. → Преди живеех в Киев.
Special cases / exceptions: Would обикновено не се използва за past states: live, be, know и т.н. За едно отделно събитие нито used to, нито would са подходящи.
Common mistakes:
❌ I would live in Kyiv when I was a child. → ✅ I used to live in Kyiv.
❌ I would visit them last Sunday. → ✅ I visited them last Sunday.
Don't confuse with: Would тук не означава просто „ще“ или условност. В този урок означава characteristic repeated past action.
Quick summary / memory hook:
used to = repeated action + past state.
would = repeated past action.
Single event → Past Simple.

Core idea: Gerund и infinitive са различни verb patterns. Някои verbs изискват -ing, други to + V1, а някои позволяват и двете форми с промяна на смисъла.
Main rule / explanation: Gerund patterns: avoid/enjoy/suggest/finish + V-ing. Infinitive patterns: decide/hope/plan/want + to + V1. Някои verbs имат и двете модели.
Form / structure: verb + V-ing. verb + to + V1. Some verbs + both.

She suggested taking a taxi. → Тя предложи да вземем такси.
I stopped smoking. → Спрях да пуша.
I stopped to smoke. → Спрях, за да изпуша една цигара.
Special cases / exceptions: След preposition използваме -ing: interested in learning, thank you for helping.

❌ I enjoy to work here. → ✅ I enjoy working here.

❌ interested in to learn → ✅ interested in learning.

Quick summary / memory hook:

preposition → V-ing.
enjoy/suggest/finish → V-ing.
decide/hope/plan/want → to + V1.

Core idea: Past modal deduction помага да направим извод за това, което вероятно се е случило в миналото.
Main rule / explanation: Must have + V3 = силен извод. May/might/could have + V3 = възможно обяснение. Can't have + V3 = силен извод, че нещо е невъзможно или не се е случило.
Form / structure: must have + V3. may/might/could have + V3. can't have + V3.
When / why we use it: Използваме това, когато гледаме evidence и правим извод за миналото, а не когато говорим за permission или ability.
Examples:
They must have forgotten the meeting. → Трябва да са забравили за срещата.
She might have missed the bus. → Възможно е да е изпуснала автобуса.
He could have misunderstood the message. → Възможно е да е разбрал съобщението погрешно.
They can't have finished already. → Не може да са приключили вече.
Special cases / exceptions: Must have тук означава deduction, а не obligation. След have използваме V3.
Common mistakes:
❌ She might has left. → ✅ She might have left.
❌ He must go = past deduction. → Не, това е obligation; past deduction: He must have gone.
Don't confuse with: Сравни must go = трябва да отиде и must have gone = трябва да е отишъл.
Quick summary / memory hook:
must have + V3 = strong deduction.
might/could have + V3 = possibility.
can't have + V3 = strong impossibility.

Lesson / Topic: Likely, unlikely, bound, definitely, probably – probability
Core idea: В английския има няколко начина да изразим вероятност: probably, definitely, likely, unlikely и be bound to.
Main rule / explanation: Probably = вероятно. Definitely = точно/със сигурност. Likely/unlikely = вероятно/малко вероятно. Be bound to = очаква се с много висока увереност.
Form / structure: will probably + V1. be probably + place/adjective. definitely + clause. be likely/unlikely to + V1. be bound to + V1.
When / why we use it: Поставяй adverb в естествената позиция и избирай конструкцията според смисъла.
Examples:
She will probably arrive soon. → Тя вероятно скоро ще пристигне.
He is probably at home. → Той вероятно е вкъщи.
We will definitely need more time. → Със сигурност ще ни трябва повече време.
It is likely to rain. → Вероятно ще вали.
They are unlikely to agree. → Те едва ли ще се съгласят.
The new system is bound to create questions. → Новата система почти сигурно ще създаде въпроси.
Special cases / exceptions: Likely е възможно в два модела: It is likely that prices will rise. / Prices are likely to rise. Степента на увереност зависи от context; тук говорим именно за probability.
Common mistakes:
❌ She will probably comes. → ✅ She will probably come.
❌ They are likely agree. → ✅ They are likely to agree.
Don't confuse with: Probably/definitely са adverbs. Likely/unlikely/bound to са adjective-based structures.
Quick summary / memory hook:
probably = вероятно.
definitely = със сигурност.
likely = вероятно.
unlikely = малко вероятно.
bound to = много вероятно/очаквано.

Core idea: Would rather и would prefer изразяват preference, но след тях се използват различни структури.
Main rule / explanation: Would rather + V1. За действието на друг човек: I'd rather you + Past Simple. Would prefer + noun или to-infinitive.

❌ I'd prefer stay. → ✅ I'd prefer to stay.
Don't confuse with: rather + V1. prefer + noun/to-infinitive.

would rather + V1.
would prefer + noun/to + V1.
Different subject after rather → Past Simple.

Lesson / Topic: Verbs of the senses: look, sound, feel, etc.
Core idea: Look, sound, smell, taste и feel могат да описват впечатлението, което нещо създава чрез сетивата ни. В този смисъл след тях често стои adjective.

The fabric feels soft. → Материята е мека на допир.

+ like + noun for comparison.
look at ≠ look.

Core idea: Passive Voice може да се използва с почти всеки основен tense. Основата остава същата: форма на be + V3.
Main rule / explanation: Променя се формата на be, а main lexical verb остава във V3: is checked, was sent, is being tested, has been fixed, will be fixed, must be reported.

The issue must be reported. → За проблема трябва да бъде съобщено.
Special cases / exceptions: by + agent се добавя, ако performer е важен: The software was developed by a small team. Ако performer е unknown/obvious/unimportant, го пропускаме.

❌ The system is test. → ✅ The system is being tested.
❌ The problem will fixed. → ✅ The problem will be fixed.
Don't confuse with: Първо определи tense, след това постави правилната форма на be и V3.
Quick summary / memory hook:

Tense се намира в be.
Modal passive = modal + be + V3.

Lesson / Topic: Zero and first conditional and future time clauses
Core idea: Zero Conditional описва общи истини, правила, routines и предвидими резултати. First Conditional е за реалистична възможност в бъдещето.
Main rule / explanation: Zero: if/when + Present Simple, Present Simple. First: if + Present Simple, will + V1. Future time clauses с when/as soon as/before/after/until/once използват Present вместо will.
Form / structure: Zero: If + Present, Present. First: If + Present, will + V1. Time clause: when/as soon as/etc. + Present.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги за general truths/predictable results и за realistic future conditions/time sequences.
Examples:
If you heat ice, it melts. → Ако загрееш лед, той се разтапя.
When the system detects an error, it sends an alert. → Когато системата открие грешка, тя изпраща alert.
If it rains, we will stay inside. → Ако вали, ще останем вътре.
As soon as she arrives, we'll start. → Щом пристигне, ще започнем.
Special cases / exceptions: В future time clause обикновено не се поставя will: When I finish, I will call you. Result clause може да съдържа will, modal или imperative.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will finish, I will call you. → ✅ When I finish, I will call you.
❌ If you heat ice, it will melt. → За general truth стандартно е If you heat ice, it melts.
Don't confuse with: Zero = general/predictable result. First = realistic future possibility.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Zero: Present → Present.
First: Present → will.
Future time clause → Present, not will.

Lesson / Topic: Second and third conditionals – unreal conditionals
Core idea: Second Conditional показва unreal/hypothetical present or future. Third Conditional показва unreal past и въображаемия му резултат.
Main rule / explanation: Second: if + Past Simple, would + V1. Third: if + Past Perfect, would have + V3. Could/might могат да заменят would, ако е нужен смисъл на ability/possibility.
Form / structure: Second: If + V2, would + V1. Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги за hypothetical/unreal situations: Second — now/future, Third — past.
Examples:
If I had more time, I would learn another language. → Ако имах повече време, щях да уча друг език.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train. → Ако бяхме тръгнали по-рано, щяхме да хванем влака.
If I had more time, I could help. → Ако имах повече време, бих могъл да помогна.
Special cases / exceptions: Не поставяй would в if-clause: If I had known..., not If I would have known.... Past form в Second не означава непременно past time.
Common mistakes:
❌ If I would have known... → ✅ If I had known...
❌ If I had more time, I would have helped yesterday. → Third Conditional: If I had had more time, I would have helped.
Don't confuse with: Гледай time: unreal now/future → Second; unreal past → Third.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Second → if + Past, would + V1.
Third → if + Past Perfect, would have + V3.

Lesson / Topic: Wishes and regrets – I wish / if only
Core idea: I wish и if only показват, че искаме ситуацията да е различна. Формата зависи от това дали говорим за настоящето, миналото или поведение/ситуация, която искаме да се промени.
Main rule / explanation: Present wish: wish + Past Simple. Past regret: wish + Past Perfect. Annoying situation/change in behaviour: wish + would.
Form / structure: wish + V2. wish + had + V3. wish + would + V1.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги за нереално желание в настоящето, съжаление за миналото или желание някой/нещо да се промени.
Examples:
I wish I knew the answer. → Жалко, че не знам отговора.
If only I had more time. → Само да имах повече време.
I wish I had studied harder. → Жалко, че не съм учил по-усърдно.
I wish you would stop interrupting. → Иска ми се да спреш да ме прекъсваш.
Special cases / exceptions: Wish + would обикновено се отнася до поведението на друг човек или до ситуация, която говорещият иска да промени. За unreal present не поставяме просто Present Simple.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish I know the answer. → ✅ I wish I knew the answer.
❌ I wish I had more time yesterday. → За past regret: I wish I had had more time.
Don't confuse with: Present unreal → Past Simple. Past regret → Past Perfect. Want behaviour/situation to change → would.
Quick summary / memory hook:
wish + Past = искам настоящето да е различно.
wish + had + V3 = съжаление за миналото.
wish + would = искам промяна.

Core idea: Participles -ing и -ed могат да се използват като adjectives. Основната разлика е между причината/ефекта и чувството/състоянието на човека.
Main rule / explanation: -ing обикновено описва нещо, което предизвиква чувство или има определен effect. -ed обикновено описва как се чувства човекът.

❌ The news was shocked. → ✅ The news was shocking.
❌ I was confusing. → ✅ I was confused.
Don't confuse with: -ing = source/cause/effect. -ed = experience/feeling.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing → предизвиква чувство.
-ed → чувства/преживява.

Core idea: Passive with reporting verbs позволява да съобщаваме информация, когато източникът е общ, неизвестен или не е важен.
Main rule / explanation: Две основни модели: It is said/believed/expected that... и person/thing + is said/believed/expected + to-infinitive. Времето на infinitive показва relationship.

Core idea: Clauses of contrast показват неочаквана разлика. Purpose clauses обясняват целта: защо правим нещо.

Core idea: Whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever и however могат да започват clauses с открито/неограничено значение: каквото и да е, който и да е, където и да е, когато и да е или независимо колко.
Main rule / explanation: Whatever = anything that. Whoever = any person who. Wherever = any place where. Whenever = any time that. However + adjective/adverb = no matter how.

When / why we use it: Използваме ги, когато конкретният вариант не е важен или значението е „няма значение кой/какво/къде/кога/колко“.

❌ Wherever + noun only. → Следващата част трябва да образува clause/idea of location.
Don't confuse with: However difficult = no matter how difficult. However alone as linking adverb = but/nevertheless.
Quick summary / memory hook:

whoever = any person who.
wherever = any place where.
whenever = any time.

Lesson / Topic: Quantifiers – all, most, both, either, neither, any, no, none
Core idea: Тези quantifiers ни помагат да говорим за цялото количество, мнозинство, два варианта, един от два, нито един от два и неопределен избор.

Lesson / Topic: Already, still, yet – What's the difference?
Core idea: Already, still и yet показват различни отношения към очакваното време: вече е станало, все още продължава или все още не е станало.
Main rule / explanation: Already = sooner than expected/before now. Still = situation continues. Yet = expected event has not happened, обикновено в questions/negatives.
Form / structure: have + already + V3. still + main verb / after be. yet often at end.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги, за да покажем, че действието вече е станало, ситуацията продължава или очакваното събитие все още не е станало.

I've already finished. → Вече приключих.
Is she already here? → Тя вече тук ли е?
I still work there. → Все още работя там.
She is still working. → Тя все още работи.
Have you finished yet? → Приключи ли вече?
I haven't finished yet. → Все още не съм приключил.
Special cases / exceptions: Position е част от pattern: already често е между auxiliary и main verb; still е пред main verb, но след be; yet често е в края.
Common mistakes:
❌ I yet haven't finished. → Неутрално: I haven't finished yet.
❌ I yet live here. → ✅ I still live here.
Don't confuse with: Still = продължава. Yet = очакваната промяна още не е настъпила. Already = случило се е по-рано/преди сега.
Quick summary / memory hook:

still = все още.
yet = още / вече? при questions и negatives.

Lesson / Topic: Needn't, don't need to, didn't need to, needn't have
Core idea: Needn't, don't need to, didn't need to и needn't have са близки, но описват различни ситуации с необходимостта.
Main rule / explanation: Don't need to / needn't = няма нужда сега. Didn't need to = нямаше нужда в миналото; само по себе си не показва дали действието е извършено. Needn't have + V3 = действието е извършено, но е било ненужно.
Form / structure: don't need to + V1. needn't + V1. didn't need to + V1. needn't have + V3.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги, за да различим липса на необходимост сега/в миналото и вече извършено ненужно действие.
Examples:
You don't need to come early. → Не е нужно да идваш рано.
You needn't wait. → Не е нужно да чакаш.
We didn't need to book a room. → Не беше нужно да резервираме стая.
You needn't have bought so much food. → Не е трябвало да купуваш толкова храна (но си купил).
Special cases / exceptions: Главната разлика: didn't need to не казва дали човекът е извършил действието; needn't have ясно показва, че действието е извършено и е било ненужно.
Common mistakes:
❌ We didn't need to buy food = задължително сме купили. → Не, това не е посочено.
❌ You needn't have bought food = не си купил. → Не, купил си, но е било излишно.
Don't confuse with: Гледай outcome: действието извършено ли е? Ако да и е било ненужно → needn't have + V3.
Quick summary / memory hook:

didn't need to = no past necessity; outcome unspecified.
needn't have + V3 = done, but unnecessary.

Lesson / Topic: Pretty, Rather, Quite, Fairly – Adverbs of degree

Lesson / Topic: When I do vs When I have done – Future time clauses
Core idea: В future time clauses след when, once, as soon as, after, before и until обикновено използваме Present, но понякога е нужен Present Perfect, за да подчертаем завършването на първото действие.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple показва обичайната последователност на бъдещи събития. Present Perfect подчертава, че първото действие ще е напълно завършено преди второто.
Form / structure: When I finish the report, I'll send it. / When I have finished the report, I'll send it.
When / why we use it: Използвай Present Simple за neutral sequence. Използвай Present Perfect, когато completion е важно. Main clause може да съдържа will.
Examples:
When I finish the report, I'll send it. → Когато завърша отчета, ще го изпратя.
When I have finished the report, I'll send it. → Когато вече съм завършил отчета, ще го изпратя.
As soon as we have received the data, we will start the analysis. → Щом получим данните, ще започнем анализа.
Special cases / exceptions: Не поставяй will в standard future time clause: When I will finish... е неправилно. Present form получава future meaning благодарение на connector.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will finish, I'll send it. → ✅ When I finish, I'll send it.
❌ When I have finish... → ✅ When I have finished...
Don't confuse with: finish = неутрална sequence. have finished = подчертано completion before next event.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Future time clause → Present, not will.
Present Simple = sequence.
Present Perfect = completion emphasized.

Lesson / Topic: Do or Make – Which is it?
Core idea: Do и make и двете могат да се превеждат като „правя“, но английският ги избира според устойчивото съчетание.

Don't confuse with: Не превеждай „правя“ дума по дума. Първо си спомни collocation.

Core idea: Have може да бъде обикновен основен глагол или auxiliary. Ролята му се определя от цялата конструкция.

Lesson / Topic: Clauses of contrast, purpose, reason and result
Core idea: Свързващите конструкции показват как една идея се отнася към друга: contrast, purpose, reason или result.
Main rule / explanation: Contrast: although/even though/whereas/while. Purpose: to/in order to/so that. Reason: because/since/as. Result: so/therefore/as a result/such...that/so...that.
Form / structure: although + clause. to + V1. because + clause. so/therefore + result. such...that / so...that.
When / why we use it: Избирай linking structure според логическата връзка, а не според буквалния превод.
Examples:
Although the task was difficult, we completed it. → Въпреки че задачата беше трудна, я завършихме.
We changed the process to reduce errors. → Променихме процеса, за да намалим грешките.
We stayed inside because it was raining. → Останахме вътре, защото валеше.
The system was overloaded, so the service became slow. → Системата беше претоварена, затова услугата стана бавна.
It was so busy that we had to wait. → Имаше толкова много работа, че трябваше да чакаме.
Special cases / exceptions: After although/even though е нужен clause. After despite/in spite of — noun или V-ing. Purpose и result отговарят на различни въпроси.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was expensive, but we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
❌ Despite it was expensive... → ✅ Despite the high price... / Despite being expensive...
Don't confuse with: Purpose = защо/с каква цел? Reason = защо? Result = какво се получи? Contrast = какво неочаквано се различава?
Quick summary / memory hook:
although/even though = contrast.
to/in order to/so that = purpose.
because/since/as = reason.
so/therefore/as a result = result.

Core idea: Когато полът на човек е неизвестен, неважен или не е посочен, modern standard English често използва singular they.
Main rule / explanation: They/them/their могат да се отнасят до един човек: someone, every applicant, a customer. Това избягва повторението на his or her.
Form / structure: someone/every + noun + they/them/their. Singular they запазва consistency в текста.
When / why we use it: Използваме го, когато говорим за човек без посочен или важен gender.
Examples:
If a customer has a question, they can contact support. → Ако клиент има въпрос, той/те може/могат да се свърже/свържат с поддръжката.
Someone left their phone here. → Някой остави телефона си тук.
Every applicant should check their email. → Всеки кандидат трябва да провери имейла си.
Special cases / exceptions: Изборът на pronoun трябва да е consistent в едно изречение/текст.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every applicant should check his or her email, then they should reply. → По-добре последователно: Every applicant should check their email, then they should reply.
❌ Someone left her phone here. (ако gender е неизвестен) → ✅ Someone left their phone here.
Don't confuse with: Singular they не означава задължително, че говорим за няколко души.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Singular they = one person with unknown/irrelevant gender.
they/them/their запазват граматиката на plural pronoun, но могат да се отнасят до един човек.

Core idea: Reflexive pronouns се връщат към subject: I hurt myself. Reciprocal pronouns показват взаимно действие: They helped each other.
Main rule / explanation: Reflexive: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Reciprocal: each other / one another.
Form / structure: subject + verb + reflexive. subject + verb + each other/one another.
When / why we use it: Reflexive — subject и object са едно и също лице. Reciprocal — двама или повече хора действат един спрямо друг.
Examples:
I hurt myself. → Нараних се.
She introduced herself. → Тя се представи.
I did it myself. → Аз сам го направих.
They helped each other. → Те си помогнаха.
The two teams respect one another. → Двата отбора се уважават.
Special cases / exceptions: Reflexive може да служи и за emphasis. Не използвай reflexive само защото звучи по-официално.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please contact myself. → ✅ Please contact me.
❌ They looked at themselves. (ако смисълът е „един към друг“) → ✅ They looked at each other.
Don't confuse with: themselves = всеки гледа себе си; each other = те гледат един друг.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Reflexive = back to subject.
Reciprocal = one another.
Emphasis: I did it myself.

Core idea: There и it могат да заемат subject position, но въвеждат различна информация. There съобщава за съществуване/поява, а it често се отнася до ситуация, време, време навън, разстояние или е preparatory subject.
Main rule / explanation: There introduces existence/occurrence. It refers to a situation, weather, time, distance or can be preparatory subject: It's important to check the data.
Form / structure: There is/are + noun. It + be/adjective/time/weather/etc. It + adjective + to-infinitive.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги, за да различим existence/occurrence от оценка на ситуация, weather, time, distance или действие.
Examples:
There is a problem with the system. → Има проблем със системата.
There are several reasons for the delay. → Има няколко причини за забавянето.
It's difficult to explain. → Трудно е да се обясни.
It's raining. → Вали.
It's five o'clock. → Пет часът е.
It's important to check the data. → Важно е да проверим данните.
Special cases / exceptions: Не бъркай There is a problem = има проблем и It is a problem = това е проблем. Preparatory it позволява real subject да се появи по-късно.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is a problem. (ако просто съобщаваме, че има проблем) → ✅ There is a problem.
❌ There is difficult to explain. → ✅ It's difficult to explain.
Don't confuse with: Има ли нещо? → there. Оценяваме ситуация/действие/weather/time/distance? → it.
Quick summary / memory hook:
there = existence/occurrence.
it = situation/weather/time/distance/preparatory subject.

Core idea: Advanced narrative tenses организират историята: main events, background, earlier events, duration before a past point, old habits и repeated actions.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = main events. Past Continuous = background. Past Perfect = earlier event. Past Perfect Continuous = duration/activity before a past point. Used to = old habits/states. Would = repeated past actions.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing. used to + V1. would + V1 for repeated action.
When / why we use it: Комбинирай формите, за да бъде ясен timeline-ът и характерът на повтарящото се действие.
Examples:
I opened the email and called the client. → Отворих имейла и се обадих на клиента.
I was driving when the message arrived. → Шофирах, когато съобщението пристигна.
They had already left when I arrived. → Те вече бяха тръгнали, когато пристигнах.
She had been waiting for an hour when the bus came. → Тя беше чакала един час, когато автобусът дойде.
I used to live there. → Преди живеех там.
Every summer, we would visit the coast. → Всяко лято ходехме на брега.
Special cases / exceptions: Would обикновено не описва past states: I used to be shy, не I would be shy. Past Perfect също не е автоматично нужен за всяко по-ранно действие.
Common mistakes:
❌ I would be shy as a child. → ✅ I used to be shy as a child.
❌ She had left before he arrived — това е достатъчно. Не е нужно всички past actions да са Past Perfect.
Don't confuse with: Първо изгради timeline, след това избери tense. For habits: used to/would.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main story.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration.
used to = past habit/state.
would = repeated past action.

Core idea: Get е изключително често срещан verb с много значения. Не може да се превежда с една-единствена дума.
Main rule / explanation: Get + adjective = become. Get + noun = obtain/receive. Get + place = arrive. Get + object + adjective = cause something to become. Get + object + V3 = arrange/cause. Get + -ing = start. Има и phrasal verbs.
Form / structure: get + adjective/noun/place. get + object + adjective/V3. get + -ing. get + particle.
When / why we use it: Използваме get според конструкцията и контекста.
Examples:
I get tired after work. → Уморявам се след работа.
I got a message. → Получих съобщение.
What time did you get home? → В колко часа се прибра?
Let's get moving. → Да тръгваме/да започваме да действаме.
Get the report checked. → Организирай проверка на доклада.
Get the room ready. → Подготви стаята.
Special cases / exceptions: Context е решаващ. Get up/get through/get along и другите phrasal verbs имат свои значения.
Common mistakes:
❌ Да учиш get = само „получавам“. → Трябва да учиш whole phrase.
❌ get to home → ✅ get home.
Don't confuse with: Гледай какво стои след get и дали има particle. Това често определя meaning.
Quick summary / memory hook:
get + adjective = become.
get + noun = receive/obtain.
get + place = arrive.
get + object + adj/V3 = cause/arrange.
get + -ing = start.

Core idea: Discourse markers показват логическата връзка между идеите и правят речта или текста по-ясни.
Main rule / explanation: Adding: also, moreover, in addition, besides. Contrast: however, nevertheless, on the other hand. Result: therefore, consequently, as a result. Example: for example, for instance. Sequence: first, then, meanwhile, finally. Conclusion: overall, in conclusion.
Form / structure: Marker + clause/sentence, position depends on marker and style. In writing punctuation matters.
When / why we use it: Избирай marker според логиката: addition, contrast, result, example, sequence или conclusion.
Examples:
The plan is expensive. However, it may be effective. → Планът е скъп. Въпреки това може да е ефективен.
Therefore, we changed the schedule. → Затова променихме графика.
For example, the first option is faster. → Например първият вариант е по-бърз.
Overall, the results are positive. → Като цяло резултатите са положителни.
Special cases / exceptions: Някои markers са по-formal от други. However е често срещан в speech/writing; moreover може да звучи по-официално. Не всички са директни синоними.
Common mistakes:
❌ Да използваш therefore като simple synonym на however. → Те показват различни logical relations.
❌ The plan is expensive however it may work. → В writing: The plan is expensive. However, it may work.
Don't confuse with: Първо определи logical relation, после избери marker.
Quick summary / memory hook:
adding → also/moreover.
contrast → however/nevertheless.
result → therefore/as a result.
example → for example.
sequence → first/finally.
conclusion → overall/in conclusion.

Lesson / Topic: Speculation and deduction – modal verbs and expressions
Core idea: Modal verbs и expressions показват степента на увереност: силен извод, възможност, невъзможност или вероятност.
Main rule / explanation: Must = strong logical conclusion. Might/may/could = possibility. Can't = strong impossibility. Past deduction: modal + have + V3. Също likely/unlikely/bound to/probably.
Form / structure: must/might/may/could/can't + V1/be. Past: modal + have + V3. likely/unlikely/bound to + V1.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги, когато говорим не за доказан факт, а за това колко уверено предполагаме.
Examples:
They must be at home. → Те сигурно са вкъщи.
They might be at home. → Възможно е да са вкъщи.
That can't be the right address. → Това не може да е правилният адрес.
They must have forgotten. → Трябва да са забравили.
She might have missed the train. → Възможно е да е изпуснала влака.
Special cases / exceptions: Must може да означава obligation или deduction. Контекстът определя: You must leave now. / You must have left already.
Common mistakes:
❌ She might has left. → ✅ She might have left.
❌ He must leave = deduction. → Не, това е obligation; deduction: He must have left.
Don't confuse with: Първо попитай: rule/obligation или evidence-based conclusion?
Quick summary / memory hook:
must = strong deduction.
might/may/could = possibility.
can't = impossible.
Past deduction = modal + have + V3.

Lesson / Topic: Inversion with negative adverbials – adding emphasis
Core idea: В formal и emphatic English начален negative/restrictive adverbial може да предизвика inversion: auxiliary се поставя пред subject.
Main rule / explanation: След Never, Rarely, Seldom, Hardly, Not only, Under no circumstances, At no time и други подобни expressions се използва inversion. Ако auxiliary няма, добавяме do/does/did.
Form / structure: Never + auxiliary + subject + verb. Rarely do we... Not only did she...
When / why we use it: Използваме го за силен emphasis и по-formal style.
Examples:
Never had I seen such a result. → Никога не бях виждал такъв резултат.
Rarely do we see such results. → Рядко виждаме такива резултати.
Not only did she solve the problem, but she also explained it clearly. → Тя не само реши проблема, но и го обясни ясно.
Special cases / exceptions: Това е formal/emphatic structure, а не обичайният разговорен word order.
Common mistakes:
❌ Never I have seen... → ✅ Never have I seen...
❌ Rarely we see... → ✅ Rarely do we see...
Don't confuse with: Начален negative/restrictive expression → провери дали е нужен inversion.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Never/Rarely/Seldom + auxiliary + subject.
No auxiliary? → use do/does/did.

Lesson / Topic: Distancing – expressions and passive of reporting verbs
Core idea: Distancing позволява да съобщаваме информация, без да я представяме като лично проверен факт.
Main rule / explanation: Използват се It is said/believed, It appears/seems, According to, Apparently и passive reporting. Тези форми са характерни за journalism, academic writing и professional reports.
Form / structure: It is said that... / It appears that... / The company is believed to... / According to... / Apparently,...
When / why we use it: Използваме ги, когато има източник на информация, но говорещият иска да се дистанцира от твърдението.
Examples:
It is believed that the company will expand. → Смята се, че компанията ще се разшири.
The company is believed to be expanding. → Смята се, че компанията се разширява.
He is thought to have left. → Смята се, че той е напуснал.
Apparently, the figures are incorrect. → По всичко личи, че цифрите са грешни.
Special cases / exceptions: Distancing не трябва да създава фалшиво усещане за certainty. Формулировката трябва да отразява наличните evidence.
Common mistakes:
❌ Да използваш It is definitely believed... без основание. → Смисълът на distancing е да покаже source/uncertainty.
❌ He is thought has left. → ✅ He is thought to have left.
Don't confuse with: Distancing = „съобщавам source/information, но не го заявявам като мой пряк факт“.
Quick summary / memory hook:
It is said/believed...
It appears/seems...
According to...
Apparently...
The company is believed to...

Lesson / Topic: Wish, rather, if only, it's time – Unreal uses of past tenses
Core idea: Wish, if only, would rather и it's time използват past forms, за да покажат нереалност, съжаление или че сега е време да променим ситуацията.
Main rule / explanation: Present unreal: wish/if only + Past Simple. Past regret: + Past Perfect. Would rather about another person + Past Simple. It's time + Past Simple може да се отнася до now/near future.
Form / structure: wish + V2. wish + had + V3. would rather + person + Past Simple. it's time + Past Simple.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги за unreal present, regret about past, preference about another person или че сега е време за действие.
Examples:
I wish I knew the answer. → Жалко, че не знам отговора.
If only I had more time. → Ако само имах повече време.
I wish I had prepared better. → Жалко, че не се подготвих по-добре.
I'd rather you didn't tell them yet. → Бих предпочел засега да не им казваш.
It's time we left. → Вече е време да тръгваме.
Special cases / exceptions: Past form тук не означава непременно past time. Тя показва distance from reality.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish I know the answer. → ✅ I wish I knew the answer.
❌ It's time we leave. → ✅ It's time we left.
Don't confuse with: Не превеждай Past формата буквално като минало. Гледай функцията: unreal, regret, preference, urgency.
Quick summary / memory hook:
wish + Past = unreal present.
wish + Past Perfect = past regret.
would rather + person + Past.
It's time + Past.

Core idea: Някои verbs приемат object, след който идва infinitive или -ing. Формата зависи от конкретния verb pattern.
Main rule / explanation: want/expect/allow/encourage + object + to V1. catch/find/keep + object + V-ing. make/let + object + bare infinitive. Remember може да промени значението според pattern.
Form / structure: verb + object + to V1. verb + object + V-ing. make/let + object + V1.
When / why we use it: Учи целия pattern: verb + object + следващата verb form.
Examples:
The manager encouraged us to apply. → Мениджърът ни насърчи да кандидатстваме.
I found him working late. → Установих, че той работи до късно.
The manager made us wait. → Мениджърът ни накара да чакаме.

I remember meeting her. → Помня как я срещнах.
I remembered to call her. → Не забравих да ѝ се обадя.
Special cases / exceptions: Remember + -ing = спомен за минало събитие. Remember + to V1 = не забравяме бъдещо/необходимо действие. Bare infinitive се използва след make/let в този pattern.
Common mistakes:

❌ They made us to wait. → ✅ They made us wait.
❌ I remember to meeting her. → ✅ I remember meeting her.
Don't confuse with: Първо определи first verb, object и pattern след object.
Quick summary / memory hook:
want/expect/allow/encourage + object + to.
catch/find/keep + object + -ing.
make/let + object + V1.

Lesson / Topic: Unless, even if, provided, as long as, etc. – Other expressions in conditionals
Core idea: Unless, even if, provided/providing и as long as изразяват различни видове условия.
Main rule / explanation: Unless = if not. Even if = резултатът няма да се промени при това условие. Provided/providing и as long as = условието трябва да бъде изпълнено.
Form / structure: unless + Present. even if + Present. provided/providing/as long as + clause.
When / why we use it: Условието се отнася до бъдещето, затова в dependent clause обикновено използваме Present, не will.
Examples:
Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train. → Ако не побързаш, ще изпуснеш влака.
Even if it rains, we'll go. → Дори да вали, ще отидем.
You can borrow it provided that you return it tomorrow. → Можеш да го вземеш, при условие че го върнеш утре.
You can stay as long as you keep the room clean. → Можеш да останеш, стига да поддържаш стаята чиста.
Special cases / exceptions: Не поставяй will след unless/if в future condition clause: Unless it rains, we'll go.
Common mistakes:
❌ Unless it will rain, we'll go. → ✅ Unless it rains, we'll go.
❌ Even if it will be difficult, we'll continue. → ✅ Even if it is difficult, we'll continue.
Don't confuse with: Unless = отрицателно условие. Even if = условието не променя result. Provided/as long as = required condition.
Quick summary / memory hook:
unless = if not.
even if = despite condition.
provided/as long as = only if condition is satisfied.

Lesson / Topic: All conditionals – mixed conditionals, alternatives to if, inversion
Core idea: Conditionals могат да комбинират различни времена и да използват алтернативи на if. В formal English е възможна inversion без if.
Main rule / explanation: Mixed conditional свързва различни time periods. Alternatives: unless, provided, as long as, on condition that, supposing, assuming. Formal inversion: Had I known..., Were I..., Should you...
Form / structure: Mixed: If + past perfect, would + present/base. Or If + past, would have + V3. Inversion: Had/Were/Should + subject...
When / why we use it: Избирай конструкцията според времето на condition/result и стила.
Examples:
If I had studied engineering, I would have a different job now. → Ако бях учил инженерство, сега щях да имам друга работа.
If I weren't so busy, I would have joined you yesterday. → Ако не бях толкова зает, вчера щях да дойда с вас.
Had I known, I would have acted differently. → Ако бях знаел, щях да постъпя различно.
Were I in your position, I would wait. → Ако бях на твое място, бих изчакал.
Should you need assistance, contact support. → Ако ви е нужна помощ, свържете се с поддръжката.
Special cases / exceptions: Inversion премахва if и поставя auxiliary пред subject. Връзката във времето трябва да остане ясна.
Common mistakes:
❌ Had I knew... → ✅ Had I known...
❌ Were I was in your position... → ✅ Were I in your position...
❌ Should you will need assistance... → ✅ Should you need assistance...
Don't confuse with: Първо определи time of condition и time of result. След това избери mixed conditional или formal inversion.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Mixed = different time periods.
Formal inversion:
Had I known...
Were I...
Should you...

Main rule / explanation: Past condition → present result: If + Past Perfect, would + V1/state now. Present condition → past result: If + Past, would have + V3.

Don't confuse with: Cause и result могат да се отнасят до различни времена.

Past cause → present result.
Present condition → past result.

Lesson / Topic: Modal verbs – permission, obligation, prohibition, necessity
Core idea: Modal verbs могат да изразяват permission, obligation, prohibition и липса на необходимост. Значението се променя според modal/semi-modal.
Main rule / explanation: Must = strong obligation. Have to = често external rule. Mustn't = prohibition. Don't have to/needn't = no necessity. Can/may = permission. Be allowed to = permission across tenses.
Form / structure: must/have to/mustn't/don't have to/needn't + V1. can/may + V1. be allowed to + V1.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги, когато трябва да изразим obligation, prohibition, no necessity или permission, включително в различни времена.
Examples:
You must wear a badge. → Трябва да носите бадж.
We have to submit the form by Friday. → Трябва да подадем формуляра до петък.
You mustn't share this password. → Не трябва да споделяте тази парола.
You don't have to attend. → Не е задължително да присъствате.
You may leave early. → Можете да си тръгнете по-рано.
We weren't allowed to enter. → Не ни разрешиха да влезем.
Special cases / exceptions: Mustn't и don't have to не са противоположности: prohibition срещу optional action.
Common mistakes:
❌ You mustn't go = „не е нужно да ходиш“. → Не: „забранено ти е да ходиш“.

Lesson / Topic: Ellipsis and substitution – Omitting or replacing words
Core idea: Ellipsis е пропускане на думи, които лесно се възстановяват от контекста. Substitution е замяна на повторяваща се структура с друга дума/израз.
Main rule / explanation: Ellipsis премахва understood material. Substitution използва one, ones, do, so, neither и други, за да избегне повторението.

I can help if you want me to. → Мога да помогна, ако искаш да помогна.
She didn't call, although she promised to. → Тя не се обади, въпреки че обеща.
I need a new laptop. So does Anna. → Имам нужда от нов лаптоп. Анна също.
I don't like the first option, but I like the second one. → Не харесвам първия вариант, но харесвам втория.
Special cases / exceptions: Ellipsis работи само когато липсващата информация може да се възстанови от контекста. Не пропускай думи, ако ще се получи ambiguity.
Common mistakes:
❌ I chose the blue report because the blue report was clearer. → ✅ I chose the blue report because it was clearer.
❌ Да се махат думи, които не могат да бъдат възстановени от контекста. → ✅ Пропускай само това, което събеседникът лесно разбира.
Don't confuse with: Попитай: може ли listener да възстанови missing words без да гадае?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Ellipsis = omit understood words.
Substitution = replace repeated material.
Context must make meaning clear.

Core idea: Cleft sentences разделят информацията на части, за да получи един елемент специален emphasis.
Main rule / explanation: It-cleft: It was + focus + who/that... Wh-cleft: What + clause + be + focus. Можем да подчертаем person, thing, time, place или reason.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced present simple and present continuous
Core idea: В advanced use изборът между Present Simple и Present Continuous зависи не само от времето, а и от това дали говорим за постоянна ситуация, временна дейност, промяна или необичаен повторяем модел.

She is working from home this month. → Този месец тя работи от вкъщи.
More companies are moving their services online. → Все повече компании преместват услугите си онлайн.
You're always interrupting me. → Ти все ме прекъсваш.
Special cases / exceptions: Някои traditionally stative verbs остават non-continuous при state meaning: understand, believe, own. Но някои verbs променят meaning и тогава могат да бъдат continuous: I'm having lunch; I'm thinking about the proposal; We are seeing more customers this year.

❌ I am understanding the problem. → ✅ I understand the problem.
❌ She owns the company, so she is owning it. → ✅ She owns the company.

Simple → stable/state/repeated.
Continuous → temporary/developing/unusual behaviour.
Meaning matters more than „now“.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced past simple, past continuous & past perfect
Core idea: Advanced work with past tenses организира narrative: кое е основната последователност, кое е background, кое е станало по-рано и кое е продължавало до миналия момент.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced modal verbs: will, would and should
Core idea: Will, would и should могат да изразяват не само бъдеще или съвет. Значението им зависи от ситуацията.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced modal verbs: can / be able to, may / might
Core idea: Can и be able to изразяват ability, но be able to е важно в други tenses/aspects и при конкретен успешен past event. May/might изразяват possibility.
Main rule / explanation: Can = ability now. Be able to е удобно във future/perfect forms. Could = general past ability. Was/were able to или managed to често са по-ясни за one specific successful past event. May/might = possibility.

Lesson / Topic: The perfect tenses: Forms and uses
Core idea: Perfect forms показват връзка между две reference points. Perfect не означава просто „минало“.
Main rule / explanation: Present Perfect свързва миналото с настоящето. Present Perfect Continuous подчертава duration/activity до настоящето. Past Perfect поставя действие пред past reference point. Past Perfect Continuous подчертава duration преди past point. Future Perfect и Future Perfect Continuous свързват completion/duration с future reference point.
Form / structure: have/has + V3. have/has been + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing. will have + V3. will have been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Главният въпрос е: спрямо кой reference point се е случило действието и важни ли са result, activity, duration или completion?

I have been working all morning. → Работя цялата сутрин.
The meeting had started before we arrived. → Срещата беше започнала преди да пристигнем.

Quick summary / memory hook:

Simple Perfect → completion/result/experience.
Perfect Continuous → activity/duration.

Lesson / Topic: Amount of vs Number of vs Quantity of
Core idea: Number of, amount of и quantity of се избират според типа noun и смисъла на количеството.
Main rule / explanation: Number of → plural countable nouns. Amount of → uncountable nouns. Quantity of → countable или uncountable, особено при измеримо количество.
Form / structure: the/a large number of + plural noun. the/a large amount of + uncountable. the/a large quantity of + countable/uncountable.
When / why we use it: Countable employees/questions → number. Uncountable money/information/traffic → amount. Measurable quantity → quantity.
Examples:
The number of employees has increased. → Броят на служителите се е увеличил.
The amount of traffic has increased. → Обемът на трафика се е увеличил.
A large quantity of water was needed. → Беше необходимо голямо количество вода.
Special cases / exceptions: Quantity of може да се използва и с countable, и с uncountable; акцентът е върху measurable quantity.
Common mistakes:
❌ the amount of employees → ✅ the number of employees.
❌ a number of money → ✅ an amount of money.
Don't confuse with: Първо: countable или uncountable?
Quick summary / memory hook:
number → plural countable.
amount → uncountable.
quantity → both, measurable.

Lesson / Topic: How to avoid double subjects in English
Core idea: В standard English clause обикновено има един grammatical subject. Не добавяй pronoun след noun, който вече е subject.
Main rule / explanation: Normal: The manager approved the request. Неутрално не е нужно: The manager, he approved... В relative clause също не добавяй излишен subject.
Form / structure: one grammatical subject per clause. Relative clause keeps its own subject/object structure.
When / why we use it: Първо намери subject и провери дали не го повтаряш с втори pronoun.
Examples:
The manager approved the request. → Мениджърът одобри заявката.
The report that I sent yesterday is ready. → Докладът, който изпратих вчера, е готов.
Тук that е допълнение към sent, а не излишен подлог.
Special cases / exceptions: В разговорна реч е възможен marked pattern My brother, he works in IT., но това не е neutral standard structure.
Common mistakes:
❌ The manager, he approved the request. → ✅ The manager approved the request.
❌ The report that I sent it yesterday... → ✅ The report that I sent yesterday...
Don't confuse with: Не добавяй pronoun, ако noun вече изпълнява ролята на subject/object в структурата.
Quick summary / memory hook:
One clause → one normal subject.
Avoid repeated subject pronouns.

Core idea: Between и among са свързани с положение/отношения в група, но не е достатъчно просто да преброиш елементите.

Quick summary / memory hook:
between → individual relationships/items.
among → within a group/distribution.

When / why we use it: Питай: някой повишава/вдига нещо? → raise. Нещо само се повишава/издига? → rise.
Examples:
They raised the price. → Те повишиха цената.
She raised her hand. → Тя вдигна ръката си.
Prices rise. → Цените се повишават.
The sun rises. → Слънцето изгрява.
The temperature is rising. → Температурата се повишава.
Special cases / exceptions: Rise е intransitive в тази basic distinction. Raise взема direct object.
Common mistakes:
❌ They rose the price. → ✅ They raised the price.
❌ She raised. → В този смисъл е нужен object: She raised her hand.
Don't confuse with:
raise = transitive.
rise = intransitive.
Quick summary / memory hook:
raise–raised–raised.
rise–rose–risen.
Object → raise.

Lesson / Topic: Remember & Forget: To Do vs Doing
Core idea: Remember/forget + to V1 се отнасят до действие, което трябва да бъде/е било извършено. + V-ing се отнася до спомена за действие, което вече се е случило.
Main rule / explanation: to-infinitive = task/action to do. V-ing = memory/experience of doing.
Form / structure: remember/forget + to + V1. remember/forget + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Сравни: Did I remember the task? vs Do I remember the event?
Examples:
Remember to send the email. → Не забравяй да изпратиш имейла.
I forgot to call him. → Забравих да му се обадя.
I remember meeting her. → Помня как се запознах с нея.
I'll never forget visiting that place. → Никога няма да забравя, че посетих това място.
I remembered to lock the door. → Не забравих да заключа вратата.
I remember locking the door. → Помня как заключих вратата.
Special cases / exceptions: Разликата не е просто във времето. Тя е в relationship between remembering and the action.
Common mistakes:
❌ I forgot meeting her. = „забравих, че трябва да се срещна с нея“. → ✅ I forgot to meet her. (забравих да го направя).
❌ I remembered meeting her. = „спомних си, че трябва да се срещна“. → ✅ I remember meeting her. (помня случилата се среща).
Don't confuse with:
to do = remember/forget the task.
doing = memory of past action.
Quick summary / memory hook:
remember/forget + to do → task.
remember/forget + doing → memory.

Core idea: Say и tell предават информация, но tell обикновено изисква object — човека, на когото се съобщава.
Main rule / explanation: Say се фокусира върху words/message. Tell се фокусира върху communicating to someone и в този reporting pattern обикновено има object.
Form / structure:
say something / say that...
tell someone something / tell someone to do something
tell the truth / tell a story / tell a joke / tell the time
When / why we use it: Първо определи дали receiver of message е назован.
Examples:
She said that she was tired. → Тя каза, че е уморена.
She told me that she was tired. → Тя ми каза, че е уморена.
He told us the truth. → Той ни каза истината.
He told a joke. → Той разказа виц.
Tell me the time, please. → Кажи ми колко е часът, моля.
Special cases / exceptions: След tell често назоваваме receiver, но не винаги. Устойчивите tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke, tell the time се използват без него.
Common mistakes:
❌ He said me the truth. → ✅ He told me the truth.
❌ He told me to the truth. → ✅ He told me the truth.
❌ She told that she was tired. → ✅ She said that she was tired. / She told me that she was tired.
❌ He said a joke. → ✅ He told a joke.
Don't confuse with:
say = words/message.
tell = tell someone.
Quick summary / memory hook:
say something.
say that...
tell someone something.
tell someone to do.

Lesson / Topic: Try to do vs Try doing
Core idea: Try to do и try doing могат да означават „опитай“, но focus-ът е различен.
Main rule / explanation: Try to do = направи усилие да извършиш действие. Try doing = експериментирай с действие/метод, за да видиш дали работи.
Form / structure: try + to + V1. try + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Питай: говорим ли за attempt to perform action или за experiment with a possible solution?
Examples:
Try to restart the computer. → Опитай да рестартираш компютъра.
I tried to contact the client. → Опитах се да се свържа с клиента.
Try restarting the computer. → Опитай да рестартираш компютъра (като начин за решение).
Try using a different browser. → Опитай с друг браузър.
Special cases / exceptions: Това не са просто две стилистични алтернативи. Infinitive подчертава effort; -ing често подсказва method/experiment.
Common mistakes:
❌ Try to restarting the computer. → ✅ Try restarting the computer.
❌ Try doing to contact the client. → ✅ Try to contact the client.
Don't confuse with:
to do = effort.
doing = experiment/method.
Quick summary / memory hook:
try to do = make an effort.
try doing = test a method.

Core idea: Until и by отговарят на различни въпроси за времето: нещо продължава до момент или трябва да приключи не по-късно от deadline.
Main rule / explanation: Until = ситуацията/действието продължава до определено време. By = deadline/latest time, до който нещо ще стане.
Form / structure: verb + until + time. verb + by + time.
When / why we use it: За continuous duration → until. За deadline/completion → by.
Examples:
I'll work until six. → Ще работя до шест.
She stayed there until Friday. → Тя остана там до петък.
Please finish it by six. → Завърши го до шест.
I'll have sent the report by Friday. → До петък ще съм изпратил отчета.
Special cases / exceptions: Until може да означава „не по-рано“, според context: Send it until Friday не е нормален начин да изразиш deadline.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please finish it until six. → ✅ Please finish it by six.
✅ I won't send it until Friday. → Тук until означава „не по-рано от петък“.
Don't confuse with:
until = continuation up to a time.
by = deadline/latest time.
Quick summary / memory hook:
until → continues to.
by → completed no later than.

Core idea: Whereas и while могат да сравняват две ситуации, но while има и други значения.
Main rule / explanation: Whereas главно противопоставя facts/characteristics. While може да показва contrast, time или понякога concession.
Form / structure: whereas + clause. while + clause.
When / why we use it: Ако ни трябва само contrast между факти → whereas. Ако използваме while, определи от context дали означава time или contrast.
Examples:
The first option is cheap, whereas the second is faster. → Първият вариант е евтин, докато вторият е по-бърз.
The first option is cheap, while the second is faster. → Първият вариант е евтин, докато вторият е по-бърз.
While I was working, she called. → Докато работех, тя се обади.
While I understand your point, I disagree. → Макар че разбирам гледната ти точка, не съм съгласен.
Special cases / exceptions: Whereas е по-formal и особено често в writing. While може да означава during the time that или contrast/concession.
Common mistakes:
❌ Да приемаш всеки while за whereas. → Не: while може да означава time.
✅ While I was working... = time, not contrast.
Don't confuse with:
whereas = contrast.
while = contrast OR time OR concession.
Quick summary / memory hook:
whereas → contrastive.
while → contrast/time/concession.

Core idea: Wish, hope и expect са свързани с бъдещи или желани ситуации, но изразяват различно отношение към reality.
Main rule / explanation: Hope = desired and realistically possible. Expect = believe something is likely/anticipated. Wish = unreal, unlikely or impossible situation или regret.
Form / structure: hope + clause/to V1. expect + noun/to V1/that-clause. wish + unreal structure.
When / why we use it: Използваме ги, за да различим realistic desire, expectation и unreal/regret.
Examples:
I hope we can finish today. → Надявам се да можем да приключим днес.
I expect the meeting to finish at five. → Очаквам срещата да приключи в пет.
I wish I had more time. → Жалко, че нямам повече време.
I wish you were here. → Жалко, че не си тук.
We wish you a pleasant journey. → Желаем ви приятно пътуване.
Special cases / exceptions: Wish не е просто синоним на hope, когато желаното събитие е реалистично възможно.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish we can finish today. → For realistic possibility: ✅ I hope we can finish today.
❌ I expect I had more time. → For unreal present: ✅ I wish I had more time.
Don't confuse with: realistic desire → hope; likely expectation → expect; unreal/regret → wish.
Quick summary / memory hook:
hope = desired + possible.
expect = likely/anticipated.
wish = unreal/regret.
